title: Pick the lantern bulb
story: A camping lantern runs on a 6 V battery and should glow with a power between 1 W and 2 W: brighter wastes the battery, dimmer is useless. The battery is happiest delivering at most 0.4 A. You have four bulbs. A glowing bulb behaves like a resistor (for example, a bulb rated 3 V and 0.3 A acts like a 10 ohm resistor when hot), so each bulb below is listed by its hot resistance. Drop one into the socket.

goals.label: the bulb glows with 1 W to 2 W
the battery delivers at most 0.4 A

hints: Power is voltage times current: P = V x I.
The whole 6 V of the battery sits across the bulb, because the closed switch is just a wire.
Preview of Phase 03: a resistor of R ohms with V volts across it lets through I = V / R amperes.
